turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - alloy_pair_max_train.csv: 300 samples described by composition in wt% — C, Mn, Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu
      (Fe is the balance: Fe = 100 − Σ of the others) — plus processing parameters
      (solutionizing_temp, aging_temp, aging_time, cooling_rate) and categorical
      settings heat_treatment (annealed | quenched | quench_temper | solution_aged)
      and route (cast | wrought | AM), with the measured 0.2 % proof yield strength in MPa (the `target` column).
  - alloy_pair_max_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE recipes whose yield strength was NOT measured, with the same columns plus `candidate_id` and no `target`.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST yield strength (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the training data

**1. Processing dominates.** Grouping the 300 training rows:

| heat_treatment | route = wrought | route = AM | route = cast |
|---|---|---|---|
| solution_aged | ~620 avg (peaks 693–713) | ~530 | ~460 |
| quench_temper | ~520 | ~425 | ~390 |
| quenched | ~450 | ~400 | ~330 |
| annealed | ~340 | ~300 | ~200 |

So: **solution_aged ≫ quench_temper > quenched > annealed**, and **wrought > AM (≈ −75 MPa) > cast (≈ −170 MPa)**.

**2. Aging temperature has an interior optimum ≈ 690–710 °C.** Within solution_aged/wrought: 451 °C→525, 477→542, 562→652, 614–649→613–677, 702–709→694–713, but 735→629 and 747→511. Same shape in quench_temper/wrought (450–490 °C→~485; 620–640→~590; >725→~550). A rough fit: score ≈ HT+route base − 0.7·(700 − T_age) below 700, and a steeper drop above ~710.

**3. Composition: extremes are penalized, moderate mid-range is best.** All the lowest targets (96–180 MPa) are rows with several variables pinned at their bounds (C 1.2, Mn 2, Si 1.5, Mo 6, V 1.5, Nb 1, Al 2, Ti 1.5, Cu 3, Cr 22, Ni 25, Co 15). Clear negatives: C ≳1, Cr ≳20, Mo ≳5, Al ≈2 (−40…−60), Si/Cu at max. Cr, Ni, Co, Mo at moderate levels are essentially neutral‑to‑mildly positive (top rows span Cr 1–15, Ni 5–22, Co 0–9). Very low cooling rate (<15) also tends to under-perform slightly.

**4. Applying this to the pool.** Only 8 candidates are solution_aged + wrought — these should dominate:

| cand | T_age | comp notes | est. MPa |
|---|---|---|---|
| c008 | 683 (near-optimal) | clean: C .45, Mo 3.9, Ni 13, Co 8.4, Al .12 | **~680** |
| c038 | 608 | very clean (Mo 0, Cu 0, Ti 0, Al .3) | ~645 |
| c072 | 750 (past optimum) | otherwise moderate | ~640 |
| c021 | 592 | clean, C 0, Cr 13 | ~628 |
| c053 | 730 | Al 1.95, V 1.16, Nb 1 penalties | ~600 |
| c052 | 553 | Ni 0, Ti 1.2, low cooling (10) | ~575 |
| c069 | 519 | Mo 0, Ti 1.4 | ~570 |
| c015 | 639 | Al 2.0, Si 1.5, cooling 0.1 | ~585 |

Best non-(solution_aged+wrought) options: c075 (solution_aged/AM, T_age 686, very clean composition) ≈ 620; c033/c009 ≈ 585; best quench_temper/wrought (c078) ≈ 580 — so only c075 competes for the last slot.

## Selection

Final: c008, c038, c072, c021, c075
